news.title: Sierra Leone FA welcomes U-15 national team home FIFA U-15 World Cup in Baku
news.lede: The SLFA has officially welcomed the Sierra Leone U-15 National Team delegation at the SLFA Secretariat following their participation in the 𝐅𝐈𝐅𝐀 𝐔-𝟏𝟓 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐮𝐩 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐁𝐚𝐤𝐮, 𝐀𝐳𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐚𝐢𝐣𝐚𝐧. The ceremony brought together SLFA officials, technical staff and members of the delegation to celebrate the team’s achievement and commend their representation of Sierra Leone on the international stage. Head of Delegation and Chairman of the Southern Region Football Association, 𝐌𝐫. 𝐉𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐩𝐡 𝐁𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭 𝐌𝐛𝐨𝐠𝐛𝐚, described the tournament as a valuable experience, praising the players for their performances.

news.title: New strategy launched to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years
news.lede: The Scottish FA and Scottish government have launched a new strategy aimed at transforming women's and girls' football over the next 10 years. Project 2035, supported by £250,000 of government funding this year, aims to increase participation levels, strengthen pathways into the game and establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035. A new taskforce will oversee the delivery of the plan, involving the Scottish government, the SFA, Scottish Women's Football, the Scottish Women's Premier League, PFA Scotland, Sportscotland and Cosla. The strategy aims to double the number of registered female players in Scotland, while also quadrupling attendances and audiences for matches.

news.title: Gambia TDS Coach Michael Spencer Reflects on Scorpion Boys’ U-15 World Cup & Festival Experience
news.lede: Reflecting on our journey at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, I am filled with immense pride—not just for the results on the pitch, but for the profound personal and collective transformation of our players. Taking a group of 15-year-olds onto the global stage is a massive undertaking. Over the course of 10 intense, high-stakes games against world-class opposition, these young player’s didn’t just play football; they grew up. Here are the biggest takeaways from the players’ journey: Sticking to our principles: Before we left, we began instilling a core set of tactical and behavioral principles.

news.title: Saliba back in training with Arsenal after being out injured since the World Cup
news.lede: LONDON William Saliba has returned to full training at Arsenal, 3½ months after his last game — in the World Cup semifinals for France. Saliba has been out of action with a back injury that didn’t require surgery but an extended period of rehabilitation, Arsenal said in July. The center back took part in a training session on Tuesday, a day before Arsenal’s Champions League match at Slavia Prague, and manager Mikel Arteta said in a pre-game news conference hours later that Saliba “is in a really good place.” “His evolution has been as expected, which is not always the case” Arteta said.

news.title: Veteran football journalist Bhasi Malaparamba, who covered eight FIFA World Cups, dies at 85
news.lede: KOZHIKODE: Veteran football journalist, author and former footballer Bhasi Malaparamba, 85, died on Tuesday following age-related ailments.A familiar name in Indian football journalism, Bhasi carved out a distinct place for himself by covering eight FIFA World Cups, from Spain in 1982 to Brazil in 2014, with official FIFA accreditation. His coverage of international football also included Euro 2008. He worked with several Malayalam newspapers and Asianet TV.Over the years, Bhasi met and interviewed some of the biggest names in football, including Pelé, Peter Shilton, Bobby Moore, Bobby Charlton and Franz Beckenbauer. His encounters with Brazilian legend Pelé in 1982 and 1990 remained among the most memorable moments of his career.Born and raised in Malaparamba, Kozhikode, Bhasi’s association with football began at an early age.

news.title: Woman charged with false statement in Cape Verde player rape investigation
news.lede: Cape Verde footballer Ryan Mendes was the subject of a rape allegation in New Zealand, which police say was "not substantiated". A woman has been charged with filing a false statement after a rape investigation that “haunted” the captain of the Cape Verde football team during the World Cup this year. Police confirmed today they have concluded their investigation into Ryan Mendes and declined to file charges against him, considering the allegation “not substantiated”. The New Zealand-based woman who accused him is set to appear in Auckland District Court next week.

news.title: Postponement of Asian Cup leaves Socceroos, FA and coach Tony Popovic at crossroads
news.lede: The most immediate question thrown up by the delay of the tournament in Saudi Arabia is what it now means for Popovic. Confirmation that the Asian Cup has been postponed until December 2027 would have caught few by surprise. But the timing of Tuesday’s announcement might have, given it came well ahead of the late November timeframe hinted at by the AFC. Yet with Houthi attacks continuing across Saudi Arabia, it felt inevitable the tournament would be deferred.

news.title: Young booters face bright future
news.lede: DT·4 November 2026 · 2:57 AM PHT·2 MIN READ. The Philippine U15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) wrapped up its maiden FIFA World Cup & Festival with a respectable 110th place out of 189 countries in the world’s biggest football tournament held in Baku, Azerbaijan in terms of participation. “Our U15’s performance tells us that our homegrowns, when given a platform, can compete well against opponents from other continents,” Philippine Football Federation (PFF) president John Anthony Gutierrez said. The Philippine side had a total of 19 goals in 10 games, highlighted by four victories against Belize (1-0) and Curacao (8-1) in the Group Stage while defeating Macau (2-0) and Aruba (5-2) in the Classification Stage.
